'''Vitaly Dmitrievich Buterin''' ({{Langx|ru|Виталий Дмитриевич Бутерин}}; born 31 January<ref>{{Cite tweet|number=1488135477593088000|user=BlockGeekDima|title=28 years ago, at 21, i became a father. What a beautiful messy complicated journey is being a parent! So much love, fear, conflict, joy, suffering, growth in that amazing human experience!! Happy birthday to a wonderful sensitive funny smart human @VitalikButerin 🥳🕺❤️🐥🔆|author=Dmitry Buterin|date=2022-01-31|access-date=2023-04-03}}</ref> 1994), better known as '''Vitalik Buterin''' ({{Langx|ru|Виталик Бутерин|links=no}}), is a Russian-Canadian computer programmer best known for co-founding [[Ethereum]]. Buterin became involved with [[cryptocurrency]] early in its inception, co-founding ''[[Bitcoin Magazine]]'' in 2011.<ref name="finley2014">{{cite magazine |last=Finley |first=Klint |date=27 January 2014 |title=Out in the open: Teenage hacker transforms web into one giant Bitcoin network |url=https://www.wired.com/2014/01/ethereum/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140212142809/http://www.wired.com/wiredenterprise/2014/01/ethereum/ |archive-date=12 February 2014 |access-date=7 February 2014 |magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]}}</ref><ref name=melendez2014>{{cite web|date=10 February 2014|last=Melendez|first=Steven|title=Could this 20-Year-Old kid make Bitcoin obsolete?|url=http://www.fastcolabs.com/3026271/could-this-20-year-old-kid-make-bitcoin-obsolete|work=[[Fast Company (magazine)|Fast Company]]|access-date=22 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301172232/http://www.fastcolabs.com/3026271/could-this-20-year-old-kid-make-bitcoin-obsolete|archive-date=1 March 2014|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2015, Buterin deployed the Ethereum [[blockchain]] with [[Gavin Wood]], [[Charles Hoskinson]], [[Anthony Di Iorio]], and [[Joseph Lubin (entrepreneur)|Joseph Lubin]].<ref name=paumgarten>{{Cite magazine |url=https://newyorker.com/magazine/2018/10/22/the-prophets-of-cryptocurrency-survey-the-boom-and-bust |title=The Prophets of Cryptocurrency Survey the Boom and Bust |last=Paumgarten |first=Nick |date=15 October 2018 |magazine=The New Yorker |archive-date=9 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200109123640/https://newyorker.com/magazine/2018/10/22/the-prophets-of-cryptocurrency-survey-the-boom-and-bust |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Early life and education==
Buterin was born in [[Kolomna]], Russia, to a Russian family.<ref name=Browne2017/><ref name="TimeBirth">{{cite magazine |last1=Chow |first1=Andrew R. |title=The Man Behind Ethereum Is Worried About Crypto's Future |url=https://time.com/6158182/vitalik-buterin-ethereum-profile/ |magazine=Time |access-date=14 September 2022 |date=18 March 2022}}</ref> His father, Dmitry, was a [[computer scientist]].<ref name=Browne2017>{{Cite news|url=http://business.financialpost.com/feature/the-cryptocurrency-prophet|title=Vitalik Buterin: The cryptocurrency prophet|last=Brownell|first=Claire|date=27 June 2017|work=Financial Post|access-date=8 March 2018|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180308123612/http://business.financialpost.com/feature/the-cryptocurrency-prophet|archive-date=8 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> He and his parents lived in the area until he was the age of six, when his parents [[Immigration to Canada|emigrated to Canada]] in search of better employment opportunities.<ref name="Uncanny">{{cite news|url=https://www.wired.com/2016/06/the-uncanny-mind-that-built-ethereum/|title=The Uncanny Mind That Built Ethereum|last=Peck|first=Morgen|date=13 June 2016|work=Backchannel|access-date=15 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170713184159/https://www.wired.com/2016/06/the-uncanny-mind-that-built-ethereum/|archive-date=13 July 2017|url-status=live|publisher=WIRED}}</ref> While in grade three of elementary school in Canada, Buterin was placed into a class for gifted children and was drawn to mathematics, programming, and economics.<ref name="Snyder">{{Cite news|last=Snyder|first=Benjamin|date=23 June 2017|title=Meet Vitalik Buterin, the 23-year-old founder of bitcoin rival ethereum|work=CNBC|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2017/06/22/meet-vitalik-buterin-the-founder-of-bitcoin-rival-ethereum.html|url-status=live|access-date=8 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180129222518/https://www.cnbc.com/2017/06/22/meet-vitalik-buterin-the-founder-of-bitcoin-rival-ethereum.html|archive-date=29 January 2018}}</ref> Buterin then attended [[The Abelard School]], a private high school in Toronto.{{sfn|Leising|2020 |pages=35–40 }} Buterin learned about [[Bitcoin]] from his father at the age of 17.<ref name=Uncanny/> In 2012, Buterin won a bronze medal in the [[International Olympiad in Informatics]] in Italy.<ref>{{Cite web |url= http://www.ioi2012.org/competition/results-2/ |title= Results {{!}} IOI 2012 |website= www.ioi2012.org |access-date= 21 July 2016 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160304084951/http://www.ioi2012.org/competition/results-2/ |archive-date= 4 March 2016 |url-status= live }}</ref>

After high school, Buterin attended the [[University of Waterloo]]. There, he took advanced courses and was a research assistant for [[cryptographer]] [[Ian Goldberg]], who co-created [[Off-the-Record Messaging]] and was the former board of directors' chairman of [[the Tor Project]].{{sfn|Russo|2020|p=29}}<ref>{{cite magazine |title=The Uncanny Mind That Built Ethereum {{!}} WIRED |magazine=Wired |url=https://www.wired.com/2016/06/the-uncanny-mind-that-built-ethereum/ |date=13 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170713184159/https://www.wired.com/2016/06/the-uncanny-mind-that-built-ethereum/ |archive-date=13 July 2017 }}</ref>

In 2013, he visited developers in other countries who shared his enthusiasm for code. He returned to Toronto later that year and published a [[white paper]] proposing Ethereum.<ref>{{YouTube|bIE1FH1EwZ4|Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin on good and bad ways to deal with crypto, and Spore's approach}}</ref><ref name="CanadianBusiness_Vit">{{cite magazine |url= http://www.canadianbusiness.com/innovation/change-agent/vitalik-buterin-ethereum |title= Change Agents 2016: Vitalik Buterin, Ethereum |last= Braga |first= Matthew |date= 13 October 2016 |magazine= Canadian Business |access-date= 6 June 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170607222238/http://www.canadianbusiness.com/innovation/change-agent/vitalik-buterin-ethereum/ |archive-date= 7 June 2017 |url-status= live }}</ref> He dropped out of university in 2014 when he was awarded with a grant of US$100,000 ({{inflation|US|100000|2014|fmt=eq}}){{inflation/fn|US}} from the [[Thiel Fellowship]], a scholarship created by venture capitalist [[Peter Thiel]] and went to work on Ethereum full-time.<ref name="Elliot">{{Cite web |url= http://canadaam.ctvnews.ca/why-a-20-year-old-toronto-drop-out-accepted-100-000-to-stay-out-of-school-1.1895631 |title= Why a 20-year-old Toronto drop-out accepted $100,000 to stay out of school |date= 2 July 2014 |access-date= 25 April 2016 |website= CTV |last= Elliot |first= Josh |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160601231806/http://canadaam.ctvnews.ca/why-a-20-year-old-toronto-drop-out-accepted-100-000-to-stay-out-of-school-1.1895631 |archive-date= 1 June 2016 |url-status= dead }}</ref>

On 30 November 2018, Buterin received an honorary doctorate from the Faculty of Business and Economics of the [[University of Basel]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cif.unibas.ch/en/blog/details/news/vitalik-buterin-receives-honorary-doctorate/|title=Vitalik Buterin receives Honorary Doctorate|website=cif.unibas.ch|language=en|access-date=3 July 2019|archive-date=3 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703152038/https://cif.unibas.ch/en/blog/details/news/vitalik-buterin-receives-honorary-doctorate/}}</ref>

== Career ==
=== ''Bitcoin Magazine'' ===
{{main|Bitcoin Magazine}}
In 2011, Buterin began writing for a publication called ''Bitcoin Weekly'' after meeting a person on a bitcoin forum with the aim of earning bitcoin.{{sfn|Russo|2020|p=25}} The owner offered five [[bitcoin]] (about $3.50 at the time) to anyone who would write an article for him.{{sfn|Russo|2020|p=55}} Buterin wrote for the site until it shut down soon thereafter due to insufficient revenue.<ref>{{cite web|title=Interview with Vitalik Buterin|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkeCapBOQQ0|publisher=Bitcorati, Inc.|date=10 January 2014|access-date=3 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150217161840/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkeCapBOQQ0|archive-date=17 February 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> In September 2011, Mihai Alisie reached out to Buterin about starting a new print publication called ''[[Bitcoin Magazine]]'', a position which Buterin would accept as the first co-founder and contribute to as a leading writer.{{sfn|Russo|2020|p=25}}

''Bitcoin Magazine'' in 2012 later began publishing a print edition and has been referred to as the first serious publication dedicated to [[cryptocurrencies]].<ref>{{Cite book|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OHbCBwAAQBAJ&q=Vitalik+Buterin&pg=PA156|title=The Age of Cryptocurrency: How Bitcoin and the Blockchain Are Challenging ...|last2=Casey|first2=Michael J.|publisher=[[Macmillan Publishers]]|year=2015|isbn=978-1-250-06563-6|page=88|chapter=Community|last1=Vigna|first1=Paul|access-date=18 November 2020|archive-date=5 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805181109/https://books.google.com/books?id=OHbCBwAAQBAJ&q=Vitalik+Buterin&pg=PA156|url-status=live}}</ref> While working for ''Bitcoin Magazine'', Buterin reached out to [[Jed McCaleb]] for a job at [[Ripple (payment protocol)|Ripple]] who accepted.{{sfn|Russo|2020|p=35}} However, their proposed employment fell apart after Ripple was unable to support a U.S. visa for Buterin.{{sfn|Russo|2020|p=35}}

In addition, he was from 2016 to 2024 a member of the editorial board of ''[[Ledger (journal)|Ledger]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editorial Team |url=https://ledger.pitt.edu/ojs/ledger/about/editorialTeam |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240315074433/https://ledger.pitt.edu/ojs/ledger/about/editorialTeam |archive-date=2024-03-15 |website=ledger.pitt.edu}}</ref> a peer-reviewed scholarly journal that publishes full-length original research articles on the subjects of cryptocurrency and blockchain technology.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-04-11 |title='Ledger' Becomes First Academic Journal Dedicated To Blockchain – The Technology Behind Bitcoin |url=https://www.wesa.fm/economy-business/2017-04-11/ledger-becomes-first-academic-journal-dedicated-to-blockchain-the-technology-behind-bitcoin |access-date=2025-05-18 |website=90.5 WESA |language=en}}</ref>

=== Ethereum ===
{{main|Ethereum}}
Buterin is the inventor of [[Ethereum]], described as a "decentralised mining network and software development platform rolled into one"<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/technology/0/ethereum/|title=What is ethereum and how does it differ from Bitcoin?|newspaper=The Telegraph|date=19 May 2021|last1=Benstead|first1=Sam|access-date=19 October 2020|archive-date=6 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201106232343/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/technology/0/ethereum/|url-status=live}}</ref> that facilitates the creation of new cryptocurrencies and programs that share a single [[blockchain]] (a cryptographic transaction ledger).<ref name=aron2014>{{cite news | url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg22129553.700-bitcoin-how-its-core-technology-will-change-the-world.html#.UwkwZ16cNko | access-date=22 February 2014 | work=[[New Scientist]] | title=Bitcoin: How its core technology will change the world | date=6 February 2014 | first=Jacob | last=Aron | issue=2955 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222023511/http://www.newscientist.com/article/mg22129553.700-bitcoin-how-its-core-technology-will-change-the-world.html#.UwkwZ16cNko | archive-date=22 February 2014 | url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://futurethinkers.org/vitalik-buterin-ethereum-decentralized-future/|title=Vitalik Buterin on Ethereum and The Decentralized Future|date=21 April 2015|website=Future Thinkers Podcast|language=en-US|access-date=13 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160518163458/http://futurethinkers.org/vitalik-buterin-ethereum-decentralized-future/|archive-date=18 May 2016|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=entrepreneur20210817>{{cite news |title=Founders' Fork: The Ethereum Architects Now Locked in Battle |url=https://www.entrepreneur.com/article/380431 |last=Jain |first=Aman |work=Entrepreneur |date=17 August 2021 |access-date=19 August 2021 |archive-date=18 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210818211950/https://www.entrepreneur.com/article/380431  }}</ref>

Buterin first described Ethereum in a white paper in November 2013.{{sfn|Leising|2020|pages=110}} Buterin had argued that bitcoin needed a scripting language for application development. But when he failed to gain agreement, he proposed development of a new platform with a more general scripting language.<ref name=tapscott2016>{{cite book |last1=Tapscott |first1=Don |last2=Tapscott |first2=Alex |title=The Blockchain Revolution: How the Technology Behind Bitcoin is Changing Money, Business, and the World |url=https://archive.org/details/blockchainrevolu0000taps |date=7 May 2016 |publisher=Portfolio |isbn=978-0-670-06997-2}}</ref>{{rp|88}}

The Ethereum white paper was circulated, and interest grew in the new protocol in late 2013 and early 2014. Buterin announced Ethereum more publicly at the North American Bitcoin Conference in [[Miami, Florida|Miami]] on 26 January. Buterin delivered a 25-minute speech, describing the general-purpose global computer<!-- p. 111 --> operating on a decentralized permissionless network, ending with potential uses for Ethereum that ranged from crop insurance to [[decentralized exchange]]s to [[decentralized autonomous organization|DAOs]].{{sfn|Leising|2020|p=129}}{{sfn|Leising|2020|p=313}}{{rp|92, 110–130}}<ref>{{YouTube|l9dpjN3Mwps|Vitalik Buterin reveals Ethereum at Bitcoin Miami 2014}}</ref>

About the Ethereum Project, Buterin said in 2020: "I am truly grateful to have the opportunity to work in such an interesting and interdisciplinary area of industry, where I have the chance to interact with cryptographers, mathematicians and economists prominent in their fields, to help build software and tools that already affect tens of thousands of people around the world, and to work on advanced problems in computer science, economics and philosophy every week."<ref name="Stu">{{cite web |title= Alumni |url= https://www.abelardschool.org/students-testimonials |website= Abelard School |access-date= 7 February 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200928181928/https://www.abelardschool.org/students-testimonials |archive-date= 28 September 2020 |url-status= live }}</ref> However, in a 2018 ''New Yorker'' article, his father suggested that Buterin was trying to avoid the focus on him as the [[philosopher king]] of the blockchain world, stating "He is trying to focus his time on research. He's not too excited that the community assigns so much importance to him. He wants the community to be more resilient."<ref name=paumgarten/>

Buterin has stated that he was driven to create decentralized money because his [[World of Warcraft]] character was [[nerfing|nerfed]], specifically by patch 3.1.0. He went on to say in his about.me bio:<blockquote>I happily played World of Warcraft during 2007–2010, but one day [[Blizzard Entertainment|Blizzard]] removed the damage component from my beloved warlock's Siphon Life spell. I cried myself to sleep, and on that day I realized what horrors centralized services can bring. I soon decided to quit.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Peck |first1=Morgen |title=The Uncanny Mind That Built Ethereum |url=https://www.wired.com/2016/06/the-uncanny-mind-that-built-ethereum/ |magazine=[[WIRED]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Good |first1=Owen |title=NFT mastermind says he created Ethereum because Warcraft nerfed his character |url=https://www.polygon.com/22709126/ethereum-creator-world-of-warcraft-nerf-nft-vitalik-buterin |website=Polygon |date=4 October 2021 |access-date=6 October 2021}}</ref></blockquote>

=== Open-source software ===
Buterin has contributed as a developer to other open-source software projects.<ref name=finley2014/> He also contributed to DarkWallet<ref>{{Cite book |chapter-url= https://books.google.com/books?id=OHbCBwAAQBAJ&q=Vitalik+Buterin&pg=PA156 |title= The Bitcoin Big Bang: How Alternative Currencies Are About to Change the World |date= 2015 |publisher= [[Wiley Publishing]] |isbn= 978-1-118-96366-1 |page= 156 |chapter= Smart Money, set it and forget it |last1= Kelly |first1= Brian |access-date= 18 November 2020 |archive-date= 5 August 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210805181049/https://books.google.com/books?id=OHbCBwAAQBAJ&q=Vitalik+Buterin&pg=PA156 |url-status= live }}</ref> by [[Cody Wilson]], Bitcoin [[Python (software)|Python]] libraries,<ref>{{Cite book |title= Mastering Bitcoin: Unlocking Digital Cryptocurrencies |last1= Antonopoulos |first1= Andreas M. |chapter= #4. Keys, Addresses, and Wallets |page= 82 |isbn= 978-1-4493-7404-4 |date= 20 December 2014 |publisher= [[O'Reilly Media]] |chapter-url= https://books.google.com/books?id=IXmrBQAAQBAJ&q=Vitalik+Buterin&pg=PA82 |access-date= 18 November 2020 |archive-date= 5 August 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210805181119/https://books.google.com/books?id=IXmrBQAAQBAJ&q=Vitalik+Buterin&pg=PA82 |url-status= live }}</ref> and the cryptocurrency marketplace site Egora.<ref name=melendez2014/>

=== Ethereum Russia ===
As Buterin was recognizing the economic and political relevance of the Ethereum enterprise for his native Russia, he met with President [[Vladimir Putin]] on 2 June 2017, at the [[St. Petersburg International Economic Forum]] (SPIEF). Putin stated that he "supported the idea of establishing ties with possible Russian partners".<ref>Sebastian, Clare (Nov 2017) [https://money.cnn.com/2017/11/07/technology/russian-bitcoin-farm/index.html "Russia eyes cryptocurrency dominance"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180720195251/https://money.cnn.com/2017/11/07/technology/russian-bitcoin-farm/index.html |date=20 July 2018 }} ''CNN Tech''. Retrieved 20 July 2018.</ref>

===Work with Glen Weyl===
Buterin came into contact with economist [[Glen Weyl]] after tweeting about Weyl's proposal for a new [[wealth tax]].<ref>{{cite magazine| url=https://www.wired.co.uk/article/blockchain-private-property-vitalik-buterin-glen-weyl| magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]| author=Gian Volpicelli| title=This economist wants to abolish private property using blockchain| date=14 June 2018| access-date=4 January 2021| archive-date=27 January 2021| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210127160055/https://www.wired.co.uk/article/blockchain-private-property-vitalik-buterin-glen-weyl| url-status=live}}</ref> The two then wrote a manifesto ''Liberation Through Radical Decentralization'', where they highlighted the common ground between Buterin's work on cryptocurrencies and Weyl's work on market-based solutions to social problems.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://medium.com/@VitalikButerin/liberation-through-radical-decentralization-22fc4bedc2ac| title=Liberation Through Radical Decentralization| author=Vitalik Buterin and Glen Weyl| date=21 May 2018| access-date=4 January 2021| archive-date=26 February 2021| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226095825/https://medium.com/@VitalikButerin/liberation-through-radical-decentralization-22fc4bedc2ac| url-status=live}}</ref> Collaborating with Zoe Hitzig, a PhD student at [[Harvard University|Harvard]], they published a paper in 2019 entitled ''A Flexible Design for Funding Public Goods''. The paper sets out a method for optimal provision of public goods, using a version of [[quadratic voting]].<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/abs/10.1287/mnsc.2019.3337|journal=Management Science|author=Vitalik Buterin |author2=Zoe Hitzig |author3=Glen Weyl |date=2 July 2019|title=A Flexible Design for Funding Public Goods|volume=65|issue=11|pages=5171–5187|doi=10.1287/mnsc.2019.3337|arxiv=1809.06421|s2cid=198858039|access-date=4 January 2021|archive-date=5 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805181115/https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/abs/10.1287/mnsc.2019.3337|url-status=live}}</ref> As of August 2022, quadratic funding had been used to allocate over $20 million to open-source software projects, primarily through Gitcoin Grants.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.gitcoin.co/blog/gitcoin-grants-quadratic-funding-for-the-world | title=Gitcoin Grants – Quadratic Funding for the World &#124; Gitcoin Blog }}</ref>

=== Artificial intelligence ===
In May 2021, Buterin donated $665 million to the [[Future of Life Institute]], a nonprofit which, amongst other things, seeks to mitigate the [[existential risk from artificial intelligence]]. Buterin worries that AI could become the new dominant species on Earth, and may "end humanity for good".<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024-03-26 |title=The little-known AI group that got $660 million |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2024/03/25/a-665m-crypto-war-chest-roils-ai-safety-fight-00148621 |access-date=2025-01-09 |website=POLITICO |language=en}}</ref>

=== Philanthropic efforts against the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine ===
Buterin spoke out in support of Ukraine amid its [[Russian invasion of Ukraine|invasion by Russia in 2022]]. On the first day of the invasion, Buterin tweeted that "Ethereum is neutral, but I am not",<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1496695587495981056 |user=VitalikButerin |title=Reminder: Ethereum is neutral, but I am not. |first=Vitalik |last=Buterin}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Laurent |first=Lionel |date=3 March 2022 |title=When War Hits, Even Crypto Can't Stay Neutral |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2022-03-03/amid-russian-invasion-of-ukraine-even-crypto-can-t-stay-neutral?leadSource=uverify%20wall |publisher=Bloomberg}}</ref> and that the attack was a crime against both the Ukrainian and the Russian peoples.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1496695424387801090 |user=VitalikButerin |title=Очень расстроен решением Путина отказаться от возможности мирного решения спора с Украиной и вместо этого начать войну. Это преступление против украинского и русского народа. |first=Vitalik |last=Buterin |trans-title=Very upset by Putin's decision to abandon the possibility of a peaceful resolution to the dispute with Ukraine and instead go to war. This is a crime against the Ukrainian and Russian people. |lang=ru}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=27 February 2022 |title=Ukraine raises over $15 mn in crypto post Russian invasion |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/international/ukraine-raises-over-15-mn-in-crypto-post-russian-invasion-122022700309_1.html |publisher=Business Standard}}</ref> A few days later, he responded to a tweet by [[RT (TV network)|RT]]'s editor-in-chief [[Margarita Simonyan]] with "{{lang|ru|иди на хуй}}" {{gloss|go fuck yourself}}. She had claimed that people who said they were ashamed to be Russians because of Moscow's actions against Ukraine were, in fact, not Russians at all ("{{lang|ru|Если вам сейчас стыдно, что вы русские, не волнуйтесь, вы - не русские.}}").<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1498012161439932430 |user=VitalikButerin |title=иди на хуй |first=Vitalik |last=Buterin}}</ref>

Buterin has donated crypto to projects supporting the country and endorsed projects helping Ukraine through "cryptophilanthropy". These include Ukraine DAO,<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1497632851445043200 |user=VitalikButerin |title=An opportunity to support Ukrainians here! Proceeds go to civilian efforts helping Ukrainians suffering from the war. |first=Vitalik |last=Buterin}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Urian |first=B. |date=27 February 2022 |title=Binance Announces $10 Million Donation to Ukraine: Ethereum Creator Vitalik Announces UkraineDAO |url=https://www.techtimes.com/articles/272352/20220227/breaking-binance-announces-10-million-donation-ukraine-ethereum-creator-vitalik.htm |website=Tech Times}}</ref> in which his father Dmitry is one of the key-holders on its multi-signature crypto safe.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Locke |first=Taylor |date=31 March 2022 |title=Ethereum's Russian-born cofounder has been quietly supporting a DAO that raised $8 million in crypto for Ukraine. His dad is even more involved. |url=https://fortune.com/2022/03/31/ukraine-dao-crypto-donations-vitalik-buterin/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221128125339/https://fortune.com/2022/03/31/ukraine-dao-crypto-donations-vitalik-buterin/ |archive-date=28 November 2022 |access-date=28 November 2022 |work=Fortune}}</ref>
